trickyParts: Only two of the nine both-sides files conflicted, and both were one collision: the contract number. Everything else main's release touched merged clean.
The generated bundle is the file a merge is most likely to corrupt silently. It was rebuilt from source and checked with `check-dist`, never resolved by reading the diff.
discoveredComplexity: This is the second forward merge of this branch and the second changed fingerprint, each for a real reason — #2070's restructure, then main's release taking the contract number. A long-lived branch against a repository that releases daily should expect the number it reserved to be taken, and the collision note's rule (renumber when the published release declaring the number lacks your shapes) is what decides it rather than seniority of the branch.

The reviewer's round 14 found nothing wrong with the change and everything wrong with the forge state, and said so plainly. That is the cheapest kind of round and it is worth naming: a conflicting head silently stops every later check, so a reviewer reading mergeability before reading code saves the tree a wasted pass.
